In today’s competitive market, the efficiency and effectiveness of purchasing activities play an essential role for all organizations to achieve success. One of the appropriate approaches that help attain this matter is group purchasing. In group purchasing, the buyers pool their purchasing volumes and information and share their resources to take advantage of economies of scale, which result in increasing bargaining power, obtaining lower prices, saving costs, and eliminating redundant efforts and activities (Karabağ and Tan, 2018, Schotanus et al., 2010).
